quickStart.item_10: For an immediate emergency involving police, fire, or ambulance, call 111.
quickStart.item_23: For urgent health advice that is not an emergency, call Healthline on 0800 611 116.
quickStart.item_17: For poison advice, call the National Poisons Centre on 0800 764 766.
quickStart.item_14: For brief emotional support, call or text 1737. If someone is in immediate danger, call 111.
quickStart.item_57: Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, KiwiSaver, pensions, and essential liabilities.
quickStart.item_67: Use official bereavement and provider processes. Do not access accounts or use credentials without authority.
quickStart.item_40: Keep the export encrypted and never store passwords, PINs, myIR/RealMe credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_105: Publicly funded health and disability services have eligibility rules. ACC is a separate scheme for injuries and acceptance and support depend on its rules.
legalNotes.item_01: A New Zealand EPA for property and an EPA for personal care and welfare are distinct. EPA authority ends on death; an executor's authority comes from the will and any required court grant.
legalNotes.item_25: Estate administration, probate, tax, relationship property, and trust questions can depend on the facts and may require High Court or professional steps. Confirm with Govt.nz, Inland Revenue, and a qualified New Zealand adviser.
legalNotes.item_101: Poison advice: National Poisons Centre: https://poisons.co.nz/

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in New Zealand. Confirm representative authority and current legal, tax, and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - New Zealand
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; individual legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Follow official registration guidance, identify the executor or administrator, notify relevant agencies and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere.0: Follow the official death-registration and certificate process.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor; check whether a High Court grant or other authority is required.
startHere.2: Notify Inland Revenue, Work and Income, ACC, banks, insurers, employers, and KiwiSaver or pension providers as appropriate.
startHere.3: List assets, debts, regular bills, and claims; confirm responsibility before changing payments or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of contacts and documents supplied. Never use another person's myIR, RealMe, banking, or device credentials.

legalFramework.0: Govt.nz death, wills, probate, and estate processes.
legalFramework.1: Inland Revenue final individual and estate tax responsibilities.
legalFramework.2: Different enduring powers of attorney for property and personal care and welfare; an EPA does not appoint an executor and ends on death.
legalFramework.3: KiwiSaver, NZ Super, ACC, insurance, relationship property, and trust rules depend on programme and personal circumstances.

0.definition: A person named in a will who is responsible for administering the estate, subject to applicable law and any required grant.

1.definition: A legal appointment for property or personal care and welfare decisions during a person's lifetime; it is separate from a will and does not continue after death.

2.definition: A High Court grant confirming an executor's authority to administer an estate when required.
